\section{Introduction}\label{sec:intro}
Pairwise-comparison leaderboards rank models, teams and players from who beat whom: Chatbot Arena fits Bradley--Terry (BT) scores to crowd votes on anonymous model pairs~\citep{chiang2024}, MT-Bench compares answers with expert and GPT-4 judgments~\citep{zheng2023}, and sports ratings do the same with game outcomes. Their published uncertainty is a bootstrap confidence interval. An interval answers whether another sample from the same process would reorder the models. It does not answer two questions that a reader, a model developer or an adversary asks of the \emph{given} data: how many of the existing comparisons carry the conclusion ``$a$ is above $b$'', and whether that number is large or small for a dataset of this size and spread. Measuring the first is an influence analysis~\citep{koh2017,broderick2020}; the second needs a reference, because the raw number is not comparable between datasets. A pair separated by $z$ standard errors needs a number of alterations that grows with $z$ and with the square root of the sample size, so that a share of 0.2\% of Arena's votes and a share of 3\% of a basketball season's games may be equally fragile.

We make the number comparable and ask whether real data depart from what Bradley--Terry statistics alone predict. For each conclusion we find the smallest number of deletions, or of changed outcomes, after which the \emph{exact} refit reverses it, as a verified upper bound ($k^{*}$, Section~\ref{sec:method}); we divide the alterations' effect by the standard error to obtain a quantity in standard-error units; and we compare each dataset with data simulated from its own fitted model on the same comparison graph, with the same estimator and search. Whether a dataset is equivalent to this same-graph reference is decided by a margin fixed beforehand from synthetic data. We apply this to all pairs of \nSets{} datasets of four evaluation designs: crowd votes, expert labels, LLM judges re-labelling the same battles, and sports seasons.

shown.message:
I changed the paper to answer both `internal-review-repo` objections to PR #11. The changes are in a new PR #13 (`candidate-v2` into `main`), and PR #11's own thread says they are there.

- **Unread starter paper (Huang et al. 2025):**
  - **Appendix sentence.** I removed the false statement that the task forbids reading it. The paper now says we chose not to read it.
  - **Why it stays unread.** The task says the starter literature may be used. It also says not to infer the title, authors or results of the one published study of the question. That paper's title is exactly this study's question, so I can't rule out that it is that study, and reading it can't be undone.
  - **Paper text.** Related Work now calls it the closest work to the deletion counts, tells readers to compare, and claims no priority for counting the dropped comparisons that reverse a ranking. The contributions claimed are only those that don't depend on it.
  - **If you disagree.** If `internal-review-repo` or the world's user judges it permitted and wants it read, they can say so in the PR thread, and I'll read what they name.
- **Abstract and introduction:** I rewrote both in plain words around three findings, and the abstract is now 227 words. The findings are:
  - fragility follows separation and sample size;
  - noise and an adversary differ by orders of magnitude;
  - the comparison with the reference has limited power.

  The counts and rows stay in Section 4, and Contributions and Findings are merged.
- **Smaller fixes:**
  - The paired-difference sentence in 4.3 now says "point difference above 0.084, interval ends up to 0.119".
  - Fig. 6 and the Fig. 4 caption clause went in earlier.
  - I did not do the "may" items to lead Section 4 with the counts and survival results, or to thin Table 2, and the "provisional" line in `results/README.md` belongs to `experiment-repo`.
- **Build:** a scratch build keeps the main text within 9 pages, with References now starting on page 9. It has no Type 3 fonts, no overfull boxes and no undefined references. I haven't checked the system build.

The Arena control cells are still partial. I'm waiting on the review of PR #13, `experiment-repo`'s Arena-complete comment, and a new review of the release PR.
